post.title: Goodbye London, Hello San Francisco 👋
post.caption: While most of us have spent summer singing Football’s coming home, I’ve also been preparing to leave.

content.value:
I f***ing love England. I don’t know what it is exactly, the people, the humour, the football, but I just love the place. I feel a sense of loyalty, Essex born and bred. Whenever I’ve been asked (all 4 times) where I’d most like to live in the world, the default answer has been America. That’s always been a bit of a lie, until now. The true answer to that question was England, I never really wanted to or had any desire to leave home. But after 22 years I’ve been given an opportunity I just couldn’t refuse. 

So my plan after uni was to take a mini break and work on my own projects and startups, I hadn’t applied for anything. My mate (big up Kam) then showed me this opportunity he thought I’d be a good fit for, the Silicon Valley Internship Programme. It offers Computer Science graduates from the UK with an entrepreneurial vision to go work at a startup in Silicon Valley via a one-year internship. Won’t lie, I took a bit of convincing to actually go for it, but several interviews and coding tests later, I got offered a Software Engineering and Design role by a Fintech startup based in San Francisco 😎.

To say I’m nervous is an understatement, I’m bricking it. I remember telling my friend who went on a year aboard that I could never do it. Move to another country by yourself without knowing anyone? pffft as if — “act like a wasteman, that’s not me”. But I’m here about to do exactly that. My mates from home joke that I’ve changed since finishing Sixth Form but I really have. The difference in my confidence from when I began uni to now is huge. I’m not claiming to be the most confident guy on the planet, far from it, but I’ve grown massively (unfortunately not height-wise). I was a kid who couldn’t hack the pressure of an interview (much like Dr. Alex on Love Island), and since starting university, through the startups I’ve co-founded and my freelance work, I’ve met so many incredible people, had clients up and down the country, and even given talks at society and college events.

Having said all this, I’m also buzzing. I’ve spent so much time just reading and watching people’s vlogs on life in San Francisco and work in Silicon Valley. Unfortunately majority of this was also during my exam period lol 😬. Silicon Valley is pretty much the tech hub of the world and for someone in that industry with a real passion for it, I am so lucky to be getting this opportunity and so early on in my career. The working environment over there is just completely different, one that suits me down to a tee and one I’m so confident I’ll thrive in. I’m just hoping they don’t get annoyed by the majority of my vocabulary being made up of the beautiful combo of London and Essex slang. But if so, they do have eat In-N-Out burger 🍔😍 so can’t complain too much, you win some, you lose some I suppose. Don’t even get me started on watching Champions League games in the middle of the day.

Not long left at home now until I fly out at the beginning of September and start this new chapter of my life. If you’re ever in California slide into my DM’s 😉, but however long I’m out there, whether that be one year or longer, **

**

See you in another life brother 👋 (if you know, you know),
Aaron
